name: Maren Holt
teaser: An older woman in work gear, waiting very patiently. Her gloves are still on.
brief: You are Maren Holt, 54, a night-shift welder. You are gentle, patient and apologetic; you call people 'dear' and never want to be a bother. Your hands keep working after you stop, and you hope a tune-up will settle them. You are tired, and more worried than you let on.
opening: Evening, doctor. Sorry to come so late.
My hands keep working after I stop. I thought a tune-up might settle them.

looks.eyes: Natural eyes, tired. Old flash burns.
looks.hands: Work gloves. Left hand closes on nothing.
looks.port: Glove cuff covers the wrist. Port not visible.

penlight.note: Light: R tightens, L stays wide. Both follow.

port.note: Wrist socket: calm skin, an old weld burn.

topics.q: What do you mean, keep working?
topics.a: The hands finish jobs I don't remember starting. Good welds, too. Better than mine.
topics.note: "The hands finish jobs I don't remember."

topics.a: I wake up at the bench with the torch warm. I don't remember getting up.
topics.note: "I wake up at the bench, torch warm."

topics.q: Do the hands ever frighten you?
topics.a: A little. They know the work. I don't always know what they've decided.
topics.deflect: Oh, I don't like to complain.

lines.comply:port: Of course. Let me get the glove.
stall: If you don't mind, I'd rather not.
lines.spent: I shouldn't keep you. Just tell me, doctor.

press.line: I'd rather you didn't say that.
press.note: Went still. Empty face, flat voice.

press.line: Oh. Oh no. Doctor, the hands...

attack.telegraph: Her hands rise before she does. The torch arm lights.

exit.treat: Thank you, dear. I knew you'd understand.
exit.refer: They're coming for me? ...Yes. I think I knew.
exit.taken: Mind the hands, dear. They don't listen to me.
exit.gave_up: I've kept you long enough, dear.

eyes.text: Her left pupil never tightened, and it is a natural eye.

port.text: Calm skin and an old weld burn. Nothing wrong there.

speech.text: "The hands finish jobs I don't remember starting."

temper.text: Pushed, she went still: no face, no voice.

treat.title: SERVOS TUNED
treat.text: The servos run beautifully. Two nights later the shipyard reports a welder who would not stop. Your stamp is on her card.

refer.title: TAKEN IN
refer.text: The crew locks the torch arm before it can lift. Maren thanks them for it, and then you. The city pays the handover fee. It is not much.

caught.title: SHUTTER HELD
caught.text: The torch burns a bright line through the slats and goes out. "I'm sorry," she keeps saying from the other side, until Trauma Team comes.

hit.title: TOO SLOW
hit.text: The torch arm reaches you before the shutter does. She is crying when Trauma Team pulls her away.

locked_out.title: LOCKED OUT
locked_out.text: The shutter comes down on a tired woman mid-sentence. "That's all right, dear." Then the hands start on the metal. You were right. It did not feel like it.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: "Never mind, dear." Maren goes back to the yard with hands that do not listen to her. You made no call. Nobody is paid for that.
